clue.text: Entertainment one can get at in there

indicators.note: the clue says the little word goes in the larger word that follows, so one is placed inside the other

explanation.surface: A show that anyone can get to by going inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'get at' as 'reach'; 'in' is the container signal, and 'one can get' is only a link meaning the place where you get it.
explanation.definitionFit: Drama on stage is a form of entertainment, and the playhouse or the art form both carry this name.

clue.text: What this sharper wins at bridge, three times

parts.note: the winning units in bridge are tricks
ter is Latin for three times, used on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A card cheat's winnings at bridge, three times over.
explanation.walkthrough: TER is Latin for 'three times', familiar from old prescriptions ('ter in die').
explanation.definitionFit: A sharper is a swindler or cardsharp, a cheat who deceives people.

clue.text: Object — manipulating sore back.

parts.note: an end is an object or aim

indicators.note: manipulating the word sore means handling and rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: Treating a sore back by manipulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reads as part of the body but is the verb, to support.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a candidate or plan is to support it publicly.

clue.text: They render unto our seizers

parts.note: echoing 'render unto Caesar', the seizers who take our money are the revenue collectors, and those who render are citizens who pay

explanation.surface: A biblical echo of rendering unto Caesar what is Caesar's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seizers' sounds like 'Caesars' (Matthew 22:21); the seizers are the tax authorities.
explanation.definitionFit: Citizens who hand over revenue to the government render it unto those who seize it.

clue.text: He was swindled by a smooth character

definitions.text: He was swindled by a smooth character

parts.words: He was swindled by a smooth character
parts.note: in Genesis, Jacob, 'a smooth man', cheated his hairy elder twin of his birthright and blessing

explanation.surface: A man conned by a slick operator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smooth character' sounds like a slick con man; in Genesis 27:11 Jacob is literally 'a smooth man', unlike his hairy brother.
explanation.definitionFit: The hairy elder son of Isaac lost his birthright and blessing to his smooth-skinned twin Jacob.

clue.text: They prove that children aren't unbearable

definitions.text: They prove that children aren't unbearable

parts.words: They prove that children aren't unbearable
parts.note: read 'unbearable' literally as 'not able to be borne': the women who give birth show that children can indeed be borne

explanation.surface: A defence of children against the charge that they are insufferable.
explanation.definitionFit: Women who bear children are living proof that children are bearable in the sense of being carried and delivered.

clue.text: Can one make light of this character's romantic work ?

definitions.text: Can one make light of this character's romantic work ?

parts.words: Can one make light of this character's romantic work ?
parts.note: this person arranges marriages, and the word also names a maker of the sticks you strike to make a flame

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone's love affairs can be treated lightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make light of' means 'treat as trivial', but a maker of matches literally makes light.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who pairs up couples for romance also shares a name with a manufacturer of matches.

clue.text: Rents that tend unhappily to fall

definitions.meaning: drops of water shed from the eyes when one is sad

explanation.definitionFit: Rips in cloth and the drops shed when crying share this spelling, though they are said differently.

clue.text: Recluse's humble contribution before starting

indicators.note: 'starting' places the word for 'before' at the start, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
the widow's mite in the Gospels is the humble offering of a poor woman

explanation.surface: A hermit's modest offering before setting out.
explanation.walkthrough: The widow's mite (Mark 12:42) is the proverbial small but sincere gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit is a religious solitary, someone who withdraws from society.

clue.text: She sees the States in opposite directions

indicators.note: 'in' says the country sits inside, between the two compass points

parts.note: south and north are opposite points of the compass, S and N
USA stands for the United States

explanation.surface: A woman travels the United States from end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a common woman's name, so she is a girl or woman called this.

clue.text: A pointer to banned books

definitions.meaning: the forefinger, used for pointing, or a pointer on a scale or in a book
the Roman Catholic Church's list of prohibited books

explanation.definitionFit: The forefinger is the digit we point with, and the Vatican's former catalogue of forbidden reading was called by this same name.

clue.text: Those who swallow up small industrialists ?

definitions.text: Those who swallow up small industrialists ?

parts.words: Those who swallow up small industrialists ?
parts.note: the 'small industrialists' are tiny industrious insects that live in colonies, and the swallowers are creatures that feed on them

explanation.surface: A business story about corporate predators gobbling up little firms.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests asset-strippers taking over small companies; the industrious little workers are insects, proverbial for hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: These long-snouted mammals feed by lapping up colonies of tiny, busy insects.

clue.text: One of the Chosen People

parts.note: Chosen (Choson) is the old name of the land of the Morning Calm, so a native of that country is one of its people

explanation.surface: A member of the people whom scripture describes as chosen by God.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital C points to the Jewish people; in fact Chosen (Joseon) was the dynasty and historical name of Korea.
explanation.definitionFit: Chosen was the historical name of that East Asian peninsula, so a citizen of it belongs to the people of Chosen.

clue.text: He paints badly for an actor

indicators.note: done badly, the letters of the two words are put together in a muddled order

explanation.surface: A poor painter would be better off going on the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Thespis was the legendary first Greek actor, so a performer on stage is named after him.

clue.text: Clubs for lawmen

parts.note: clubs here are short heavy sticks, carried by police officers

explanation.surface: Social clubs set up for lawyers or police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' suggests societies; here they are cudgels carried by police.
explanation.definitionFit: Police officers in Britain traditionally carried short wooden batons as weapons.

clue.text: Subject of an autobiography?

parts.note: an autobiography is about its writer, so its topic is the definite article followed by the first-person object pronoun, run together

explanation.surface: A question about what a life story written by its subject covers.
explanation.walkthrough: Split after its third letter, the answer is what every autobiography is about: the author's own self.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic or subject is the main idea of a piece of writing, and split in two the word names the author's self.

clue.text: Of course, it's proverbially Old English

definitions.text: Of course, it's proverbially Old English

parts.words: Of course, it's proverbially Old English
parts.note: 'course' is a course of a meal, and the song 'The ... of Old England' makes this dish the proverbial national fare

explanation.surface: A remark about something that is, naturally, as English as can be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' reads as 'naturally' but means a dish served as a course; the 18th-century song 'The Roast Beef of Old England' made it a patriotic symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint of oven-cooked sirloin is the traditional Sunday dinner and a famous emblem of England.

clue.text: They might cause a stir, those speculators

indicators.note: 'might cause' a stir suggests disturbance, so the letters of the words that follow are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Speculators who might create a disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' looks like part of the phrase 'cause a stir', but its letters join THOSE as the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: People who form hypotheses or conjectures about how things work are speculators in thought.

clue.text: A trying bit of work for the cook ?

definitions.text: A trying bit of work for the cook ?

parts.words: A trying bit of work for the cook ?
parts.note: 'trying' is testing rather than tiresome: a cook samples a dish before serving

explanation.surface: A tiresome job in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trying' seems to mean irksome, but the cook is trying (sampling) the food in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: A sample taken in advance gives a hint of what is to come, like a chef sampling a dish.

clue.text: Send a rose perhaps-to make Carmen better?

indicators.note: 'perhaps' tells us the letters may be put another way, so the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to a suitor wooing the opera's heroine, Carmen, with flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carmen' is read as CAR MEN, motorists, who would be better with good judgement on the highway.
explanation.definitionFit: Awareness of traffic and hazards is what makes motorists safer drivers.

clue.text: An award for degeneration

parts.note: an is the article a
a trophy is an award such as a cup

explanation.surface: A prize given for decline.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasting away of a body part or tissue is a form of degeneration.

clue.text: Duck colour that is turned down

indicators.note: turned down means rejected, but here it says the pieces are turned round and read in reverse

parts.note: red is a colour
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A duck's colour that has been rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned down' turns REDIE right round, giving EIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large sea duck famed for the soft down used in quilts.

clue.text: One stone no slimmer wants to lose

definitions.text: One stone no slimmer wants to lose

parts.words: One stone no slimmer wants to lose
parts.note: slimmers want to lose a stone (14 pounds) in weight, but nobody wants to lose a precious gem

explanation.surface: A dieter's goal of losing a stone in weight.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of body weight equal to 14 pounds; here it is a gemstone.
explanation.definitionFit: The hardest precious gem, worn in rings, is one jewel nobody wishes to mislay.

clue.text: Like a balloon or its intoxicated pilot?

definitions.meaning: a balloon must be sealed so no gas escapes
a pilot who is drunk ('tight') up in the air

explanation.definitionFit: A balloon is sealed against leaks, and a drunk balloonist would be tipsy while aloft.

clue.text: Wrong a girl

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: Mistreating a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of order or faulty is awry or incorrect.

clue.text: The child's. identified, in short, as 8

parts.note: the apostrophe-s is short for is
Sue is the short form of the woman's name entered at 8 down

explanation.surface: A child has been identified by a shortened name.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of "child's" stands for IS; 8 down gives the full name, and its short form is SUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring or descendants are a person's progeny, as in 'died without children'.

clue.text: He avoids class-consciousness

parts.note: 'class' is a school class, so he avoids being conscious in class by skipping school altogether

explanation.surface: A man who steers clear of snobbery about social rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'class-consciousness' suggests social snobbery; the class here is a school lesson he dodges.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil who stays away from school without permission avoids his lessons.

clue.text: Employer is all for change, to be sure

indicators.note: 'all for change' is set up as a person keen on reform, but signals that the letters of sure are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boss who is certainly keen on reform.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who employs a tool or service makes use of it.

clue.text: Kipling's. name for triumph and disaster

definitions.text: Kipling's. name for triumph and disaster

parts.words: Kipling's. name for triumph and disaster
parts.note: Kipling's poem 'If' says to meet triumph and disaster 'and treat those two' frauds 'just the same'

explanation.surface: A literary question about what Kipling called triumph and disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The line from Kipling's 'If' runs 'If you can meet with Triumph and Disaster / And treat those two impostors just the same'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling called success and failure deceivers, frauds pretending to matter more than they do.

clue.text: Their goods are impaired when they're oiled.

definitions.text: Their goods are impaired when they're oiled.

parts.words: Their goods are impaired when they're oiled.
parts.note: read the retailers plus 'oiled' as one word: goods that are ...-... are damaged from handling and display

explanation.surface: Merchandise spoilt by being greased.
explanation.walkthrough: Add 'oiled' to the answer and you get SHOP-SOILED, the term for stock damaged from being on display.
explanation.definitionFit: Retail outlets hold stock, and their goods become marked or faded when left too long on show.

clue.text: A tendency to start 'suddenly if spoken to?

definitions.text: A tendency to start 'suddenly if spoken to?

parts.words: A tendency to start 'suddenly if spoken to?
parts.note: to shy is to start suddenly, as a horse does; a bashful person flinches when addressed

explanation.surface: A nervous habit of jumping when someone speaks to you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' as a verb means to start back in alarm, like a startled horse, so the timid quality is a tendency to shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Timidity makes a bashful person recoil in discomfort when addressed.

clue.text: What is left is due to rise for a change

indicators.note: 'for a change' asks for the letters to be changed about into a new order

explanation.surface: Whatever remains is about to go up, for once.
explanation.definitionFit: A remainder or leftover is what stays behind after the rest is removed.
